L132@P2:  Cardiac Toxicity: Cardiovascular events, including heart failure, cardiomyopathy, and myocardial L135@P2: specific additional risk factors for SUNitinib-induced cardiomyopathy apart from the drug-specific L136@P2: effect have been identified in the treated patients. Use SUNitinib with caution in patients who are at L137@P2: risk for, or who have a history of, these events. L138@P2: Baseline and periodic evaluations of LVEF should also be considered while the patient is receiving L139@P2: SUNitinib. In the presence of clinical manifestations of CHF, discontinuation of SUNitinib is L140@P2: recommended. The administration of SUNitinib should be interrupted and/or the dose reduced in L141@P2: patients without clinical evidence of CHF but with an ejection fraction <50% and >20% below L142@P2: baseline. L143@P2:  QT prolongation: QT interval prolongation may lead to an increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias L144@P2: including Torsade de pointes. Torsade de pointes has been observed in <0.1% of SUNitinib-exposed L145@P2: patients. L160@P3:  Hypertension: Patients should be screened for hypertension and controlled as appropriate. L161@P3: Temporary suspension is recommended in patients with severe hypertension that is not controlled L162@P3: with medical management. Treatment may be resumed once hypertension is appropriately L163@P3: controlled. L164@P3:  Aneurysms and artery dissections: The use of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) pathway L165@P3: inhibitors in patients with or without hypertension may promote the formation of aneurysms L166@P3: and/or artery dissections. Before initiating SUNitinib, this risk should be carefully considered in L167@P3: patients with risk factors such as hypertension or history of aneurysm. L168@P3:  Hypothyroidism: Baseline laboratory measurement of thyroid function is recommended in all L169@P3: patients. Patients with pre-existing hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism should be treated as per L170@P3: standard medical practice prior to the start of SUNitinib treatment. During SUNitinib treatment, L171@P3: routine monitoring of thyroid function should be performed. Patients who develop thyroid L172@P3: dysfunction should be treated as per standard medical practice. Hypothyroidism has been observed L173@P3: to occur early as well as late during treatment with SUNitinib. L174@P3:  Skin and tissue disorders: L175@P3: o Skin discolouration, possibly due to the active substance colour (yellow), is a very common L176@P3: adverse reaction occurring in approximately 30% of patients. Patients should be advised that L177@P3: depigmentation of the hair or skin may also occur during treatment with SUNitinib. Other L178@P3: possible dermatologic effects may include dryness, thickness or cracking of the skin, blisters, or L179@P3: occasional rash on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet. The above reactions were not L180@P3: cumulative, were typically reversible and generally did not result in treatment discontinuation. L181@P3: o Cases of pyoderma gangrenosum, generally reversible after drug discontinuation, have been L182@P3: reported. Severe cutaneous reactions have been reported, including cases of erythema L183@P3: multiforme (EM) and cases suggestive of Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal L184@P3: necrolysis (TEN), some of which were fatal. If signs or symptoms of SJS, TEN, or EM L185@P3: (e.g.progressive skin rash often with blisters or mucosal lesions) are present, SUNitinib treatment L186@P3: should be discontinued. If the diagnosis of SJS or TEN is confirmed, treatment must not be restarted. In some cases of suspected EM, patients tolerated the reintroduction of SUNitinib L187@P3: therapy at a lower dose after resolution of the reaction; some of these patients also received L188@P3: concomitant treatment with corticosteroids or antihistamines. L189@P3:  Wound healing: This treatment may impair wound healing and temporary interruption of treatment L190@P3: is recommended in patients undergoing major surgical procedures. L191@P3:  Haemorrhage and tumour bleeding: Haemorrhagic events, some of which were fatal, reported L192@P3: through post-marketing experience have included gastro-intestinal, respiratory, urinary tract and L193@P3: brain haemorrhages. Patients receiving concomitant treatment with anticoagulants) may be L194@P3: periodically monitored by complete blood counts (platelets), coagulation factors (PT/INR) and L195@P3: physical examination. L196@P3: DRUG INTERACTIONS: L197@P3:  Co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided because it may decrease L198@P3: SUNitinib plasma concentration. L199@P3:  Limited clinical data are available on the interaction between SUNitinib and BCRP inhibitors and the L200@P3: possibility of an interaction between SUNitinib and other BCRP inhibitors cannot be excluded. L201@P3:  Co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided because it may increase the L202@P3: plasma concentration of SUNitinib. L179: L180: PREMEDICATIONS: Not usually required L181: L182: OTHER SUPPORTIVE CARE: No specific recommendations L183: L184: ADVERSE EFFECTS / REGIMEN SPECIFIC COMPLICATIONS: L185: L186: The adverse effects listed are not exhaustive. Please refer to the relevant Summary of Product Characteristics for full details. L187: • Hepatic effects: Cases of hepatic failure (including fatalities) have been reported during use of PAZOPanib. Administration of PAZOPanib to patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment should be undertaken with caution and close monitoring. L188: PAZOPanib is not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin > 3 x ULN regardless of any level of ALT) Exposure at a 200mg dose is markedly reduced, though highly variable, in these patients with values considered insufficient to obtain a clinically relevant effect. In clinical studies with PAZOPanib, increase in serum transaminases (ALT, aspartate aminotransferase [AST]) and bilirubin were observed). L189: In the majority of the cases, isolated increases in ALT and AST have been reported, without concomitant elevations of alkaline phosphatase or bilirubin. Patients over 60 years of age may be at greater risk for mild (>3xULN) to severe (>8xULN) elevation of ALT. Patients who carry the HLA-B*57:01 allele have an increased risk of PAZOPanib-associated ALT elevations. Liver function should be monitored in all subjects receiving PAZOPanib, regardless of genotype or age (see Regular Tests). L190: • Hypertension: Patients with hypertension should exercise caution while on PAZOPanib. Blood pressure should be well controlled prior to initiating treatment. Treatment with PAZOPanib should be discontinued if there is evidence of hypertensive crisis or if hypertension is severe and persists despite anti-hypertensive therapy and PAZOPanib dose reduction. L191: • Cardiotoxicity: The risks and benefits of PAZOPanib should be considered before beginning therapy in patients who have pre-existing cardiac dysfunction. The safety and pharmacokinetics of PAZOPanib in patients with moderate to severe heart failure or those with a below normal LVEF has not been studied. Patients should be carefully monitored for clinical signs or symptoms of congestive heart failure. Baseline and periodic evaluation of LVEF is recommended in patients at risk of cardiac dysfunction. L192: QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes have also been reported. PAZOPanib should be used with caution in patients with any relevant cardiac history, or those taking anti-arrhythmics or other medicines that may prolong the QT interval. Ensure electrolytes are maintained within normal range. When using PAZOPanib, base line and periodic monitoring of electrocardiograms and maintenance of electrolytes (e.g. calcium, magnesium, potassium) within normal range is recommended. L193: • Muscle pain: Myalgias and muscle spasms can occur in patients treated with PAZOPanib L194: L195: • Hypothyroidism: Thyroid dysfunction, in particular hypothyroidism, may occur with this treatment. Patients with hypothyroidism should be treated as per standard medical practice prior to the start of PAZOPanib treatment. Monitor for signs and symptoms of thyroid dysfunction and manage as clinically appropriate. L196: L197: L198: L199: L201: L202:

L203: NCCP Chemotherapy Regimen L204: L205: - **Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)/Pneumonitis:** ILD, which can be fatal, has been reported in association with PAZOPanib. Monitor patients for pulmonary symptoms indicative of ILD/pneumonitis and discontinue PAZOPanib in patients developing ILD or pneumonitis. L206: L207: **DRUG INTERACTIONS:** L208: - Concomitant treatment with strong inhibitors of CYP3A4, P-glycoprotein (P-gp) or breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) should be avoided due to risk of increased exposure to PAZOPanib. Selection of alternative concomitant medicinal products with no or minimal potential to inhibit CYP3A4, P-gp or BCRP should be considered. L209: - Concomitant treatment with inducers of CYP3A4 should be avoided due to risk of decreased exposure to PAZOPanib. L210: - Concomitant administration of PAZOPanib with uridine diphosphate glucuronosyl transferase 1A1 (UGT1A1) substrates (e.g. irinotecan) should be undertaken with caution since PAZOPanib is an inhibitor of UGT1A1.
